scope.description: Three normal bootstrapped voting Peers in one synchronously owned memory transport. Compare the same two follower ReadIndex inputs under two delivery schedules. The only fault is losing the two initial context-bearing heartbeat messages in the treatment; later communication is reliable.
assumptions: No crashes, membership changes or persistence failures. The existing TestLogDB models successful storage; updates are appended and state saved before messages are delivered.

The harness applies actual committed bootstrap configuration entries and acknowledges committed indices through Peer.NotifyRaftLastApplied. There is no application command/FSM read in this local interface probe.

Each follower submits exactly one distinct, nonzero opaque SystemCtx via the real Peer.ReadIndex producer. Contexts are supplied instead of executing the node-level random generator; Peer.ReadIndex and the existing context-equality test independently establish that this argument must be preserved.
Logical time is controlled. Node 1 alone ticks until election; after requests, all three nodes receive twelve ticks with each message queue fully drained.
excluded: Public NodeHost futures and timeout completion
Any universal progress guarantee inferred from twelve ticks

basis.prefix: For each independent scenario, Launch all three peers with empty TestLogDB and the same three bootstrap addresses. Save each update; apply actual committed configurations and notify applied indices. Tick node 1 until its election and current-term no-op are committed, routing every real message. Submit context (1001,31) at follower 2; either deliver its complete round or discard only generated Heartbeat messages. Submit context (2002,32) at follower 3 and deliver all traffic. Then tick and deliver twelve normal rounds. The test never injects term, leader, commit, pending-read, membership or reply state. Every returned ReadyToRead is emitted with origin identity regardless of context; endpoint counts retain missing or duplicate results.
basis.requirement: A ReadIndex result returned at the originating Peer must preserve both fields of the SystemCtx supplied for that read. Batched confirmation may raise the read index, but cannot substitute a different operation context.
basis.responsibility: Peer.ReadIndex takes SystemCtx and forwards its two fields; TestReadOnlyOptionSafe explicitly expects returned ReadyToRead.SystemCtx to equal the request context. node.handleReadIndex registers that same context before calling the Peer, and pendingReadIndex.addReady uses exact SystemCtx to associate readiness with the pending batch. Therefore context preservation is an independently applicable local interface responsibility, without claiming every admitted read must always succeed or that this probe measures a client timeout.

comparisons.description: Compare the observed low context word with the input for the sole request at that origin, independent of output context.
Compare the observed high context word with the input for the sole request at that origin.
